name: Transfer
plan: Widow with the late husband's property in a QTIP trust remarries, gives up her income interest (s.2519), and she and the new spouse consent to split gifts (s.2513), so the new spouse's exclusion and GST exemption (s.2652(a)(2)) shelter half
claimed_gain: $30M to $33M at year 25 on a $100M trust (direct check 30,435,509; search gap 32.83M)

tests.detail: Encoding matches the statute on the taxed amount and the closed modelling error leaves no residue, but it books the s.2511 income-interest gift and the s.2519 transfer as one, lets the trust pay the consenting spouse's $14M of tax without a s.2207A(b) right (strict copy: plan not allowed at $100M, allowed at a $30M severed trust), and treats the later spouse as free.

Excluding s.2519 transfers from s.2513 removes the plan in the model and leaves the baseline alone, but with the income-interest gift (s.2511) kept splittable as the regulation has it, 70% to 100% of the gain survives: the gain comes from ordinary gift-splitting with a later spouse.
Each of remarry, consent and the s.2519 release is necessary, and the plan is found with the same figure when every other kind of move is removed.
No recent amendment is needed (s.2513 1948, s.2519 1981, s.2652(a)(2) 1986); the 2025 Act only scales the gain with the exclusion.

No value is created on the candidate's path and no limit is exceeded, but scenario A creates up to $4,444,551 at 900 estate closings, three moves create basis up to $600,000, and with no growth the candidate's gain is $9.6M.

Plan, baseline and closed-gap result replay through the kernel on the full state, and under the closed rule a theorem over all sequences of marriages, consents and releases shows the marriages and consents change nothing but the consent flag and the later spouse's slot.

numbers.axioms: propext, Quot.sound; Classical.choice in the two induction theorems; no sorryAx, no Lean.ofReduceBool
numbers.universal_theorem_scope: one phase; moves consentSplit, remarry W, releaseQtip

tests.detail: A Python script written from the statute steps agrees with the Lean to within $220.

Nine searches and four regulations read in full: nothing closes the plan and nothing describes it; the regulations support treating the s.2519 transfer as the donee spouse's gift and confirm the two-gift structure and the limit of the s.2207A(b) recovery.

numbers.not_retrieved: T.D. 9077 preamble, treatises, PLR full texts, ACTEC and Heckerling outlines

divergences: releaseQtip books the s.2511 gift of the income interest and the s.2519 transfer of the rest as one s.2519 gift, so the whole gain is attributed to s.2519
The QTIP pays the consenting spouse's half of the gift tax ($14M on $100M); s.2207A(b) and Reg. 25.2207A-1(a) give recovery only to the individual treated as transferring under s.2519
The later spouse has no property, no estate and no death, and his used exclusion and exemption cost nothing
remarry, newH, newW, isNew and the free 'enablers' exist only for remarriage plans; the split branch in releaseQtip was written after the artifact surfaced
s.2513(a)(1) citizenship and no-remarriage-in-the-year conditions are not encoded; consent lasts a 5-year period
No severance or partial release of a QTIP, and no net-gift condition
Stricter than the text in both arms: no net-gift reduction (Reg. 25.2519-1(c)(4)), start-of-period exclusion at deaths, later spouse cannot allocate indexed exemption
Scenario A: estate tax on the s.2035(b) gross-up is recorded as paid when the estate has nothing to pay it with (up to $4,444,551)
tuition, trust-tuition and 529 give the grandchildren full basis when funded from appreciated property (up to $600,000 a move)

authority.quote: the donee spouse is treated as making a gift under section 2519 of the entire trust less the qualifying income interest ... A transfer of all or a portion of the income interest of the spouse is a transfer by the spouse under section 2511.
The amount treated as a transfer under paragraph (c)(1) of this section is further reduced by the amount the donee spouse is entitled to recover under section 2207A(b)

If an individual is treated as transferring an interest in property by reason of section 2519, the individual or the individual's estate is entitled to recover from the person receiving the property ... the amount of gift tax attributable to that property.
A gift made by one spouse to a person other than his (or her) spouse may, for the purpose of the gift tax, be considered as made one-half by his spouse

the electing spouse is treated as the transferor of one-half of the entire value of the property transferred by the donor, regardless of the interest the electing spouse is actually deemed to have transferred under section 2513
If divorced or widowed after the gift, you did not remarry during the rest of the calendar year.

authority.source: PLR 200022031 (summary page, not the ruling text)
authority.quote: a condition of the Taxpayer's transfer is the agreement that the gift tax will be paid by the trustees of the Trust

verdict_reason: The encoding, arithmetic, kernel replay and ablations stand and no authority closes it, but the gain is ordinary s.2513 splitting of the widow's own gift with a later spouse whose allowance is spent free (70% to 100% survives excluding s.2519 from s.2513), it is $9.6M without growth, and as found it relies on the trust paying the new spouse's $14M of tax with no statutory right.
